question: What's the difference between the 2011 and 2026 model risk guidance?
final_answer:
Here is a summary of the key differences between the 2011 and 2026 model risk guidance, based on the retrieved documents.

The 2026 guidance (SR 26-2 / OCC Bulletin 2026-13) is a full replacement of the 2011 guidance (OCC Bulletin 2011-12 / SR 11-7), driven by supervisory experience, industry feedback, and technological advances in modeling (occ_2026_13.txt, index=3). The 2011 guidance applied broadly across all banks; the 2026 guidance explicitly states it is most relevant to banking organizations with over $30 billion in total assets, reflecting a more tailored, risk-based supervisory approach (sr_26_2.txt, index=2). Smaller banks below $30 billion are still covered but typically under their own internal governance practices (sr_26_2.txt, index=3).

The 2026 guidance also narrows the definition of "model," explicitly excluding simple arithmetic calculations such as those in spreadsheets and deterministic rule-based processes with no statistical or economic theory underpinning them (sr_26_2.txt, index=4). The 2011 guidance did not draw these same explicit exclusions.

Additionally, the 2026 guidance explicitly carves out generative AI and agentic AI models as outside its scope due to their novelty and rapid evolution, with a separate request for information planned to address them (occ_2026_13.txt, index=4). The 2026 guidance also explicitly states it does not set enforceable standards, so non-compliance will not result in supervisory criticism (sr_26_2.txt, index=2).
